text:
alex: alert: soft-ECC error rate spiked ~3x in us-west2 GPU pool over the last 20m. Several hosts marking 'degraded' and autoscaler started evicting pods — ~18% capacity drop. cc @maya @pj

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-42 - GPU error surge in us-west2 :rotating_light:

maya: looking now — telemetry shows per-card soft-ecc counters steadily incrementing, not seeing multi-bit/hard ECC yet. Lots of correctable errors.

pj: grabbing kernel logs; lots of repeated GPU faults and PCIe AER. snippet: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, pid 4321, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568123] pciehp 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Uncorrected error, severity=Corrected
```

alex: any correlate with recent infra pushes or kernel updates? last kubelet roll was ~04:12Z.

maya: checked packages — no kernel or kubelet changes in that window, but nv-host driver v2.1.3 was rolled to a small canary set ~3h ago. rolling that back on canaries now.

infra-bot: Deployment rollback started for nv-host v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2 on canary subset (20 hosts)

pj: suggestion — hold provisioning/new node creation for us-west2. Autoscaler churn is making it worse (spinning up nodes that immediately show degraded GPUs).

alex: agree. pausing autoscaler and new node creation for us-west2. @maya can you collect failing card IDs + host IDs and push to the incident bucket?

maya: uploading short dump & sample logs to s3://redwood-debug/usw2/gpu-surges/1890123456/logs.tar.gz. attached list of host/gpu IDs in the upload.

sre-lead: flagging possible thermal coupling — rack inlet temps for rack-12 were +6C above baseline starting around the spike. @ops-team pls verify fans/PSU.

kat: ops checking rack-12 now — increasing fan curves and verifying PSU currents. will report back in 15m.

maya: quick triage: error signature maps to one vendor firmware batch (firmware v4.6.1) on affected cards. opened vendor ticket #78910 and requested remote diag.

alex: for immediate customer impact mitigation: enable routing fallback for critical requests to eu-west1 and hosted nodes while we stabilize us-west2. prefer eu-west1 dedicated for low-latency customers.

pj: :thumbsup: routing change applied. ~20% of traffic shifted off us-west2. watching latency and error rates.

maya: current status: capacity drop stabilized around 12% after rollback + fan adjustments. 7 hosts had hard restarts, and 10 GPUs marked unusable pending vendor swap. vendor remote session scheduled in ~30m.

alex: good triage. keep short updates here only — if we need a full postmortem, label under INC-20260318-42. hypothesis for now: firmware + thermal edge case causing increased correctable ECC + PCIe AER, cascading into kernel GPU faults and node drains.

alex: closing loop for now — next update either vendor findings or after vendor session. thanks everyone for fast reaction :heart:
